title: Thread guards slow editor builds
body:
### Tested versions

4.5 dev 5 (but all recent 4.x)

### System information

Godot v4.5.dev (09f635562) - Linux Mint 21.1 (Vera) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-S) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700T (24 threads) - 62.54 GiB memory

### Issue description

I noticed while profiling that a lot of small functions like `is_visible()` didn't seem to be getting inlined, even with `dev=no` scons which I'm presuming is release build.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25c2c80b-873b-41d7-813e-e6288879aea7)

Turns out the thread guards are wrapped in `DEBUG_ENABLED` rather than `DEV_ENABLED` which means they are slowing down the editor, and projects run in the editor (although are compiled out of release templates).

This makes some sense, but there are situations where this micro-protection is excessive. For instance, when calling a loop that runs 100,000 times, you don't really need a thread guard check in each `is_visible()` call, you ideally want a single check outside the loop.

I had heard this discussed previously as a problem (maybe in core meeting), but I couldn't find an issue reporting it.

### Steps to reproduce

N/A

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A

## Discussion
I'm wondering whether there is some way we could add a standard way to call a version of these small functions to omit the thread guards even in editor builds. This is likely only really necessary in tight loops, but things like `data.visible` are private members of `Node` so can't be accessed directly.

Maybe we could standardize on e.g. `_is_visible()` being the no thread guard version, and `is_visible()` being the bound safe version, something like that. Or maybe something like `is_visible_NTG()` as we already use underscored convention for internal in a number of places and there could be conflicts.
